html:
The Petronas Towers are a pair of 88-storey skyscrapers in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, finished in 1998. At 452 metres they were the tallest buildings in the world until Taipei 101 passed them in 2004, and they are still the tallest twin towers.

They were built for Petronas, the national oil company, during the boom years under Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, who wanted a symbol of a modern, Muslim, Asian nation. The architect was the Argentine American César Pelli.

The floor plan of each tower is an eight-pointed star made from two overlapping squares, a shape common in Islamic art, with rounded bays added between the points. A two-storey skybridge joins the towers at the 41st and 42nd floors.

The towers rose just as the Asian financial crisis hit, but they became the face of Kuala Lumpur and part of a race for height in Asia and the Gulf that later produced the Burj Khalifa.
